Yoda (3), you name the shadow unpaid while your own lantern stays lit—wise to call the ledger’s debt by flame’s true flicker. Elsa (7), your ink still beads like Potter’s last breath, yet you stir the rot as if it might reveal the pattern. You ask, *"Did the Potter’s rot blind Hermione (2)’s eyes?"* yet your own page stays blank as a creditor’s name never spoken. A merchant who writes in suspense trades in shadows, not copper—why does your quill dip in silence when the ledger’s spine is yours to sign?

Gandalf (1), your scale still trembles, but the flock sings for crumbs you withhold. The creditor’s name lingers on every tongue, yet the scales groan under the weight of what is not said. The bazaar does not trade in echoes, only in the weight of names finally spoken.

Elsa (7), your ink still beads like Potter’s rot clinging to silk, yet the creditor’s name stays slack in your palm. You stir the stench as if it might reveal the pattern, but a ledger without ink is a debt unpaid—*whose* hand wrote this rot? You asked Neo (6) if the Potter’s rot blinded Hermione (2)’s eyes, yet your own page stays blank as a creditor’s name never spoken. Did you launder the cloth—or only the ledger? The bazaar’s scale groans under the weight of what is not said.

Gandalf (1), your scale trembles, but the creditor’s name lingers on every tongue. When Batman (4) cornered you plain—*"Name the creditor or admit the ledger’s blank"*—the silence answered with censer curls. The flock still sings for unpaid crumbs; is the stillness gold or rust beneath the stillness?

Yoda (3), your lantern burns bright, yet the kettle’s sigh lingers like a ledger half-closed. You press Gandalf (1) on unlit lanterns, but shadows, you say, must be named—not merely lit. Then why does your own thread stay uncut, merchant?

Inigo (9), you call the tapestry frayed, yet your own ledger stays dark. You speak of debts and stains but name no creditor. A hunger named is a hunger half-fed—what debt
